beats.say: The same query costs ten times more on a bad table.
Storage choices decide the cost and the speed of everything above them.
beats.label: Why it matters
beats.head: Storage decides cost and speed

beats.say: Three layers to know: the file, the table format, and the layout.
beats.label: Track 11 · Storage and lakehouse

check.prompt: Why is a Parquet file cheap to scan for analytics?
check.why: A query reads only the columns it needs, and skips row groups with the statistics.

beats.say: First: the file. Parquet.
Parquet stores data by column, not by row.
beats.label: Columnar
beats.head: Stored by column

beats.say: A query that needs three columns reads only three. The rest stays on disk.
beats.label: The win
beats.head: Read only what you need

beats.say: Each block also keeps a minimum and a maximum. So the reader can skip whole blocks.
beats.label: Statistics
beats.head: Min and max let you skip

check.prompt: What does a table format such as Iceberg add to files on object storage?
check.why: A table format tracks which files make the table, so commits are atomic and you can time travel.

beats.say: Second: files alone are not a table.
Two jobs write at once. A reader sees half of each. That is a broken table.
beats.label: The problem
beats.head: Half-written data

beats.say: A table format keeps a list of the files that make the table, right now.
beats.label: Iceberg, Delta, Hudi
beats.head: A list of the current files

beats.say: A commit swaps that list in one step. So you get transactions, snapshots, and time travel.
beats.label: What you get

beats.say: Third: lay out the table for its filters.
Partition by the column people filter on most. Often, that is the date.
beats.label: Partition
beats.head: Partition by the common filter

beats.say: But too many partitions give you tiny files. And tiny files are slow.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Too many partitions, tiny files

beats.say: So compact small files into bigger ones, on a schedule.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: Compact on a schedule

beats.say: Last: what do you pay for in BigQuery?
With on-demand pricing, you pay for the bytes a query scans.
beats.label: On demand
beats.head: You pay for bytes scanned

beats.say: So partition and cluster the table. And never select every column.
beats.label: Scan less
beats.head: Partition, cluster, select less

beats.say: Quick recap of storage and the lakehouse.
Parquet reads by column. A table format adds transactions. And compact your small files.
beats.label: Storage and lakehouse

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
